gaps.sentence: It is almost ___ to park in the city centre (POSSIBLE).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — parking is extremely difficult
gaps.explanation: The in- of 'possible' becomes im- before p: impossible. The context shows a negative meaning.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (INTERVIEW) asked her some difficult questions.
gaps.hint: the person who asks the questions (-er = doer)
gaps.explanation: The interviewer asks; the interviewee answers. The suffix -er marks the doer.

gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: She showed great ___ in dealing with the crisis (ABLE).
gaps.explanation: After 'great' a positive noun is needed: ability (-ity); 'inability' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: The campaign aims to raise ___ of road safety (AWARE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ness forms the noun: raise awareness is the fixed phrase; 'aware' is an adjective.
After 'complete' a noun is needed: darkness (-ness noun of 'dark').

gaps.sentence: He is very ___ about local history (KNOW).
gaps.explanation: 'Knowledgeable about something' means knowing a lot about it; it is the adjective form of 'knowledge'.

gaps.sentence: Her ___ (PERFORM) in the final was outstanding.
gaps.explanation: After 'Her' a noun is needed: performance (-ance noun); performers are people.
